Definition (En): A chronological series of components or phases within the geographical limits of a locality. The sequence may or may not related to an overarching archaeological period.

A temporally significant class of artifacts defined by a consistent clustering of attributes. The concept and related subcategories can be used where the chronology resource entry has been characterised by the presence and timing of a particular material cultural assemblage. Sub-categories of the material culture class include for example: Ceramics, Architectural style, Metallurgy, Wall painting, Furniture, Beads, Botanical, Fauna, Lithics, Textiles.

A clay-based product, usually divided into pottery (such as earthenware, stoneware, and faience) and porcelain (soft-paste, hard-paste, and bone china). Excavated ceramics can be used for relative dating to give an approximate date range for a site. Any relative dating technique requires accurate identification. Site occupation dates derived from excavated ceramics must be used with caution and preferably in conjunction with other sources of evidence. Example: In the MAEASaM Chronological Type, the Ceramic class is classified into 5 broad sub-categories. For example: eathernware (generally pertaining to hand-made or thrown clay vessels). Earthenware includes local pottery manufactured on-site but can also relate to earthenware that has been imported through trade networks or other historical events. In some cases, a particular temper used during the firing of vessels can be used as a distinguishable marker for a particular time period. For example, charcoal, grog, quartz, silcrete, shell, bone, etc.
Any subgroup of elements within an industry or main culture tradition, such as a ceramic tradition, that is distinguished from the whole on the basis of some aspect of appearance or composition.

Tradition is a term describing the persistence in a given area over a period of time in individual attributes, artifact types, in this case ceramics, or technologies; a culture that exists for an extended period of time and usually over an extended area.

A standardized series of metal tokens, their specific weights representing particular values, and usually stamped with designs and inscriptions. They were used in many parts of the ancient world for everyday exchange.

Earthenware is a relatively soft, low-fired, porous, ceramic.Either coarse-textured or find-grained, earth-coloured. OR A general term referring to all wares made from fired clay, including earthenware, stoneware, porcelaneous ware and porcelain - or an object made from such substances. (see https://gotheborg.com/glossary/ceramics.shtml)
The study and interpretation of ancient inscriptions, including writings, pictures, and random scratchings, incised on stone, clay, metal, or other hard surfaces.
Unit of geological time during which a rock series is deposited. It is a subdivision of a geological period. Examples: Holocene, Pleistocene, Pliocene
Era of the earth's geological history.Example: Cenozoic

A geological event is a temporally and spatially heterogeneous and dynamic (diachronous) episode in Earth history that contributes to the transformation of Earth system and the formation of geological strata. Event stratigraphy was first proposed as a system for the recognition, study and correlation of the effects of important physical or biological events on the broader stratigraphical record. Geological events as a chronology type may refer to particular glaciation events and stages, volcanic eruptions, earthquakes or other key geological events shaping earth's history

In geology, ‘periods’ are second‐order time units according to the American Commission on Stratigraphic Nomenclature's internationally agreed scheme set out in 1949 . The chronostratigraphic units making up each period are known as systems: thus the Quaternary System embraces the Pleistocene and the Holocene.

The process by which land is covered by continental and alpine glacier ice sheets or the period of time during which such covering occurred; several glaciations are required to make up an Ice Age (as the Pleistocene). The land is subject to erosion and deposition by this process, which occurred repeatedly during the Quaternary; the process modifies landscapes and affects the level of ocean basins. These periods of colder weather are also called glacials, and the warmer periods between them interglacials.

A frequently repeated assemblage of a particular material or function, i.e., flake industry, flint industry. Such an assemblage of artifacts including the same types. For example, Acheulean Industry, Wilton Industry, Lomekwian Industry. The term is mostly applied to lithic assemblages recovered from excavations.

A group of much more distantly or unrelated cultures sharing the same general families of artifact types (often used in lithic analysis) as a widely diffused and interlinked response to common factors in environment, economy, and technology.
Used to indicate that the concept is of an unknown or an uncertain type.
Works that record interviews conducted to preserve the recollections of persons whose experience or memories are representative or are of special historical or social significance.

The concept and related subcategories can be used where the chronology resource entry has been characterised by an oral or written record source. Subcategories of the Oral and Documeted time marker concept include the following: Oral history, Oral tradition, Written Record (including ship logbook, traveller account, missionary record, etc.), Epigraphy, and Coinage.

"Oral tradition has been defined as a testimony transmitted orally from one generation to another. Its special characteristics are the fact that it is oral and its manner of transmission, in which it differs from written sources. Chronology resource entries may include marine or oxygen isotopic stages such as the MIS 5, MIS 4, MIS 3, etc. The concept type can be used by where the chronology resource entry has been specified by the timing of a particular record connected by palaeoenvironmetal or palaeoclimatc analysis.

A politically independent or autonomous social unit, whether simple or complex. In the case of a complex society, such as a state, it may comprise many dependent components. The Polity concept can be used when the chronology resource entry has been characterised by the reign of a particular empire, kingdom, dyastry, state and/or complex society over a particular timespan.
Porcelain is a hard, dense, high to very high-fired, non-porous ceramic. White to grey-white in colour, fine textured body, and translucent in thin-section.
Stoneware, is a hard, dense, high-fired, non-porous ceramic. It can be coarse or find-textured and is commonly stone-coloured.

Fabric produced by spinning and weaving fibers, whether of animal or vegetable origin. Fragments may be preserved by waterlogging and tanning, by desiccation, or by corrosion of copper or bronze lying alongside. More commonly, items such as spindle whorls, weaving combs, and loom weights attest their existence. (Source: Kipfer, B. A. (2021).Encyclopedic Dictionary of Archaeology, Second Edition, pp 1375.
